transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-20
Start: 15:30 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Johnson (Redwood AE), Samira Chen (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (Atlas Head of ML), Lena Ortiz (Atlas Infra), Ravi Shah (Atlas Product)

Summary:
Quick Optimize walkthrough focusing on batching and prefix / KV cache recommendations for Atlas' conversational search workload. Covered cost model tradeoffs, latency vs throughput, dedicated vs hosted routing, and next steps for a short pilot + benchmark.

Topics: batching strategy, KV / prefix cache, cost per token model, tail latency, quantization tradeoffs, benchmark plan, security notes (SOC2, KMS).

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, we'll run through Redwood Optimize recommendations — batching and kv cache, cost model. quick intros?
[00:12] Daniel: Daniel Park, Head of ML at Atlas, hi. we're looking to lower inference cost on our conversational search product and keep p99 latency under 200ms ideally.
[00:20] Lena: lena, infra. concerned about VPC and private routing, also key management.
[00:25] Ravi: ravi, product. timeline is pilot in 2 weeks if numbers look good.
[00:30] Alex: great. Samira's our SE, she'll do deep dive on batching and caching.
[00:36] Samira: hi all. quick agenda: 1) how batching helps throughput and cost, 2) prefix/KV cache for repeated context, 3) cost model example using your expected qps, 4) next steps. quick note — apologies if transcription odd on some product names, might come out as Redwood Optimizee or Red wood.
[01:05] Samira: so, first batching. important to distinguish request-level batching (across concurrent requests) vs intra-request token batching. for your workload where you have many short queries with a shared 512-token context, batching across requests gives big wins.
[01:30] Samira: example: baseline single-request path on a 80B-equival model per-GPU, single-threaded, you get X tokens/s. with batching of 8 we typically see ~2.6-3x throughput improvement; with batch 16 up to ~3.8x depending on sequence lengths and kv cache hit rates. these are approximate, will vary with quantization and hardware.
[02:05] Daniel: so that means cost per 1M tokens drops by similar factor?
[02:10] Samira: roughly yes, but there are overheads — batching can add a bit of 95th/99th tail if you wait to fill batches. Redwood's scheduler has adaptive batching: it waits short windows (<10ms) and will flush for latency SLOs. so cost goes down but you might pay tail latency tax if you're too aggressive.
[02:35] Alex: key tuning knobs: batch target, max wait, and route by priority. for product flows where p99 is strict, we suggest smaller batch target with priority lanes for low-latency traffic.
[02:47] [crosstalk] Lena: and for dedicated vs hosted — if we go Dedicated can we control batching parameters?
[02:53] Samira: yes Dedicated exposes autoscale and batching configs; we can give you suggested presets for your percentile goals.
[03:02] Samira: next — prefix / KV cache. this is huge for conversational apps with repeated user/system context. Redwood supports both prefix caching (server-side cached token prefixes) and an MLP-backed KV cache for embeddings/partial keying.
[03:20] Ravi: can you explain difference briefly? we've seen "kv cache" in docs but unsure how it maps to our session store.
[03:27] Samira: sure. prefix cache caches the decoded token prefixes so we can skip recomputation of the early layers. KV cache (k v — sometimes transcribed as K V) caches the transformer key/value tensors for past tokens so future decoding doesn't recompute attention over the whole history. in practice kv cache gives larger perf wins for long histories; prefix cache is simpler for short shared prefixes.
[03:55] Samira: example numbers from prior Atlas-like customers: with avg session length 800 tokens and kv cache hit rate of 70%, we saw per-token compute drop ~45–60% and wall-clock latency for continuation tokens fall by ~30–40%. that maps to similar cost reductions.
[04:22] Daniel: how do you maintain cache correctness for user-specific data? we have multi-tenant sessions and privacy requirements.
[04:29] Samira: good Q. Redwood ties KV caches to session IDs and supports eviction and TTL policies; in Dedicated or Private deployments you can store cache on customer-managed volumes or encrypted object stores. we also integrate with KMS for key encryption and have audit logs for cache ops.
[04:45] Lena: any SOC2 or compliance implications?
[04:49] Alex: we have SOC2 + ISO attestation — Samira will send security whitepaper. for Private deployments we can do air-gapped and HSM/KMS integration.
[04:58] [00:05 filler] Samira: back to cost model. here's a simplified model we ran during prep: baseline (no batching, no kv cache) cost per 1M tokens = $120 (example on a/hosted 80B baseline). with batching 16 and kv cache hit 60% cost drops to about $34–40 per 1M tokens because of improved GPU utilization and fewer recomputed tokens. numbers are illustrative, your numbers depend on token lengths, qps, and quantization.
[05:35] Daniel: those are big swings — what's the main lever?
[05:38] Samira: hit rate and batch size. also quantization: 4-bit or 5-bit quantized kernels reduce memory and can increase batch concurrency; we typically see another 15–25% cost improvement with aggressive quantization while keeping quality checks.
[05:52] Ravi: what's the tradeoff on latency when enabling kv cache? we care about p50 vs p99.
[05:57] Samira: kv cache generally reduces p50 and p95 for continuation tokens. the risk is cache misses which behave like cold starts. Redwood Optimize recommends hybrid caching: keep hot prefixes pinned to memory / fast ssd and evict cold keys. also maintain a per-tenant hotset with TTL.
[06:22] [00:10] Samira: demo time — i'll share screen and show the Optimize console. apologies if some labels are off in transcript.
[06:30] Samira: opening Optimize -> Cost Models -> Batching. here you can simulate a workload: set avg seq len, qps, kv hit rate. you can toggle quantization profile and get projected cost curve and latency percentiles.
[06:47] [screen share noises] Samira: for Atlas, we set qps 80, avg seq 600, kv hit 60%. curve shows cost per 1M tokens at $38 with batch target 12 and max wait 8ms; p99 around 190ms. change batch target to 24 and cost drops to $27 but p99 rises to ~260ms.
[07:15] Daniel: can we simulate spiky traffic? our peak qps can go 6x for flash events.
[07:20] Samira: yes — the simulator supports variable qps profiles. also real runtime uses autoscaling and routing to burst pools. for spikes we recommend burst capacity and a lower-cost fallback model to maintain availability.
[07:33] Lena: if fallback model is smaller, quality will drop. how do we measure regressions?
[07:38] Alex: Redwood Eval ties quality monitoring to prompt sets and can alert if fallback model regressions exceed threshold. we can run A/B and rollback automatically.
[07:48] [small pause] Samira: a practical pilot we propose: run 48h side-by-side benchmark on Dedicated capacity with your sample traces — we instrument token-level cost and per-route latencies. results will inform recommended batch target, cache TTLs, and quantization profile.
[08:05] Daniel: timeline?
[08:07] Alex: we can provision Dedicated pilot in ~5 business days after SOW; pilot run 48h then review. since you wanted pilot in 2 weeks, this seems doable if we get sample traces today.
[08:18] Ravi: about security docs and SAML/SSO for console access?
[08:22] Samira: we support SAML, RBAC, and audit logs. will attach SOC2, pen test summary, and We have a security whitepaper.
[08:33] [transcription error] Daniel: can you also show how prefix cache interacts with retrieval-augmented generation?
[08:38] Samira: yes briefly — if you're doing RAG and have a retrieval step that adds a 200-token doc snippet per query, prefix caching helps when many queries share the same snippet (like system prompt). kv cache helps when conversation history repeats. if retrieval output differs per user, caching is less effective.
[08:58] Daniel: ok makes sense. how do you estimate cache hit rate?
[09:01] Samira: we analyze session traces to compute overlap and repeated substrings; for many search/chat workloads, 40–70% hit rates are common. we'll run sample analysis on your traces.
[09:12] Lena: anything special for multi-region? we need EU data residency.
[09:16] Samira: you can pin routes to EU region and we support Private with region-specific deployments; audit logs and KMS can be region-local.
[09:25] Alex: quick note on pricing: hosted vs dedicated — hosted is usage-based with per-token billing; Dedicated is committed monthly with lower unit cost plus reserved capacity fees. pilot pricing can be structured as trial credits against committed contract.
[09:40] Daniel: curious about competitor vendor lock and migration — we use some Anthropic endpoints today.
[09:45] Samira: Redwood plays well with multi-model routing; you can keep Anthropic for certain routes and route others to Redwood. that gives you a migration path and fallbacks.
[09:55] [11:00 timestamp noise] Samira: another technical point — KV cache warmup: first few requests cold; we can pre-warm hot prefixes during rollouts and pin important keys. also recommended to precompute embeddings for large context windows to speed retrieval + cache hits.
[10:13] Ravi: how would billing look during pilot? we prefer predictable costs.
[10:17] Alex: pilot includes a flat reserved pilot rate + usage overage; we'll include estimated token budget in proposal.
[10:24] Daniel: any limitations with our on-prem data (we have PCI scope for payments)?
[10:29] Samira: for PCI you should use Private deployment or Dedicated with customer-managed VPC and encrypted volumes, HSM for key ops. we'll share compliance docs.
[10:38] [small laughter] Alex: ok let's recap next steps.
[10:42] Alex: action items: Alex will send pricing and SOW draft; Samira will share benchmark script/runbook and security docs; Daniel will share sample traces and defined SLOs.
[10:54] Daniel: we'll aim to get traces by 11/24.
[10:58] Ravi: schedule follow-up for week of 11/29.
[11:02] Samira: thanks everyone, we'll attach the simulator screenshots and a short spreadsheet that maps batch target vs cost vs p99. note: small transcription errors possible in auto transcript.
[11:12] Alex: cool, thanks. end.
